analysis.file_name: Wolfe Research - Constellation Energy (CEG), Seguing from One Nuke Deal to the Next - Oct 7 2026.pdf
analysis.title: CEG – Seguing from one nuke deal to the next
key_insights: Constellation Energy announced a 20-year PPA with Google on 890 MW of new nuclear uprates across several PJM plants, plus a 15-year offtake for 2,700 MW of existing nuclear energy/capacity (ex-attributes). Total is 3.6 GW. No pricing was disclosed, but Wolfe says it falls within CEG's targeted $20-50/MWh premium to the PTC floor.

The Google deal shows existing generation can still be contracted. Google is described as the most stringent hyperscaler on additionality, and Wolfe understands any RBP/IRAS risk would fall on the customer.

Last week CEG announced an Amazon deal at Calvert Cliffs: 190 MW of new uprates and 500 MW of existing generation. A co-location arrangement was previously rebuffed locally, so the deal was restructured as front-of-the-meter (FTM).
CEG now has nuclear contracts with the big 4 hyperscalers. All of its nuclear uprates are now spoken for: Byron/Braidwood, Dresden, LaSalle, Limerick, Salem and Quad Cities.

About 45% of CEG's carbon-free fleet is now under long-term contract. The Google PPA is about 15% alone. Another ~5% comes from the Amazon/Calvert Cliffs PPA, the Walmart/Dresden PPA and 890 MW of existing generation contracted on the Q2 call. Nuclear plants under Illinois CMCs expiring mid-2027 are another ~25% of the fleet, and some of that output may be in the 2.7 GW existing portion of the Google PPA.

Ramps of existing volumes mostly match uprate CODs. Calvert Cliffs is 2030/2032, Google starts in 2028 but is mostly 2030+. EPS upside is longer-dated, while PJM pricing is elevated near term. The deals turn CEG into a higher-multiple infrastructure play with 15-20 years of visibility from 2030.

Wolfe's scenarios across all three deals (4.1 GW existing): base EPS upside of $1.70-2.40 at a blended $25-35/MWh premium to the PTC floor. Upside to overall earnings is $0.35-0.71 at a $5-10/MWh premium to current market, or $1.00+ versus CEG's early-year guide.
The base share of EPS rises from 65-70% toward 75%+. The uprates would be additive to earnings but come with capex.

Eagle Creek Partners (ECP) was reported by Bloomberg after the close to be selling 3M CEG shares at $294, above its last sale at $281. ECP would still own about 11M shares (3%). CEG still has 25M shares from Calpine holders under lock-up until mid-2027. Wolfe calls this a 'momentum killer'.

Wolfe rates CEG Outperform with a $395 price target (31.5% upside from $300.40). The target is 16x pro forma 2030E EPS of $19.39 plus a 50% chance of $30/MWh more margin on available nuclear generation. Official estimates and valuation have not been updated for the 5.2 GW contracted year to date (4.1 GW existing plus 1.1 GW uprates) because timing and pricing are not disclosed.

Wolfe sees the stock at about 14x 2030 EPS without pricing upside. CEG guides to a 20%+ base EPS CAGR over 2026-2029, with enhanced EPS at 30-35% of the total, and 10%+ base growth on a rolling basis longer term.
The nuclear PTC floor starts at $43.75/MWh in 2024, grows with inflation and runs through YE32. CEG is investing $1.6B to restart Crane/TMI.

market_movers.rationale: Wolfe sees CEG locking up long-term nuclear contracts at elevated rates, with 45% of the carbon-free fleet contracted and all uprates spoken for. The estimates are not yet updated for the 5.2 GW contracted year to date.
Google is the customer on the 20-year PPA for 890 MW of new nuclear uprates and the 15-year offtake of 2,700 MW of existing nuclear in PJM. Wolfe says the customer would carry RBP/IRAS risk.

sector_views.rationale: Wolfe is Market Overweight on IPPs. It says CEG is executing the IPP thesis for this power cycle by locking up long-term contracts at elevated rates.

earnings_insights: Wolfe's estimates do not yet include the new contracts. Scenario EPS upside to base earnings is $1.70-2.40 at a $25-35/MWh premium to the PTC floor. Upside to overall earnings is $0.00-0.71 at a $0-10/MWh premium to market on the 4.1 GW, based on today's forwards.
Versus the lower year-end forwards CEG assumed when it set its long-term guide, Wolfe sees an incremental $0.67 of consolidated EPS upside, if CEG could still strike prices off today's forwards.
Valuation: 24.8x 2026E P/E, 22.8x 2027E, 17.9x 2028E, 16.4x 2029E, 15.5x 2030E. EV/EBITDA is 15.1x 2026E falling to 10.0x 2030E. FCF yield is 3.9% in 2026E rising to 7.1% in 2030E.
risk_factors: Pricing and timing for the new deals are not disclosed, so earnings impact is uncertain.
Uprates add EPS but come with capex. CEG capex is $5,675M in 2026E, falling to $4,350M by 2028E.
Possible further sell-downs by ECP and the lock-up expiry of 25M Calpine-holder shares in mid-2027 are supply overhangs.
Nuclear plants under Illinois CMCs expire mid-2027, covering about 25% of the carbon-free fleet.
RBP/IRAS additionality risk on the Google deal, which Wolfe understands would fall on the customer.
charts_described: CEG price chart (FactSet, priced 10/6/26) shows the stock between roughly $237 and $404 over the last year, with CEG down 15% YTD against the S&P 500 up 14%.
vol_and_positioning: ECP, a CEG holder, was reported by Bloomberg to be selling 3M shares at $294 after the close, with about 11M shares (3%) retained. 25M shares held by former Calpine holders are under lock-up until mid-2027. Short interest is 2.8% of float.
CEG is down 15% YTD and 17% over the last twelve months, against UTY Index -2% YTD and -5% LTM and S&P 500 +14% YTD and +16% LTM. The 52-week range is $237-$404.

tension_points.bull_case: CEG has contracts with all big 4 hyperscalers, uprates are fully committed and about 45% of the carbon-free fleet is contracted at premium pricing. Base EPS mix rises toward 75%+ and the stock gets a higher infrastructure-style multiple with 15-20 years of visibility.
tension_points.bear_case: Pricing and timing are undisclosed, EPS upside is longer-dated (mostly 2030+), uprates require capex, and ECP's post-close sale of 3M shares at $294 plus the Calpine lock-up overhang weigh on momentum.

theme_stances.key_argument: CEG is locking up long-term contracts at elevated rates, with 45% of the carbon-free fleet contracted.
theme_stances.evidence: CEG is fully executing on the thesis for IPPs in this power cycle
